articleTitle: Hand Gesture Recognition based on Convolution Neural Network (CNN) and Support Vector Machine (SVM)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: Gestural communication is a type of nonverbal communication in which visible body gestures are utilised to communicate vital messages, either in place of speech or in conjunction with it. The problem of gesture division is presented as a first step toward visual hand gesture recognition, i.e., the detection, analysis, and recognition of gestures through real-time hand sequences. Visual hand recognition and motion tracking are quite challenging to solve due to their inconvenient nature. This research seeks to address the issue by determining which classification technique, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) or Support Vector Machine (SVM), is superior in recognising hand motions. The hand-skeletal was used as the features to represent the hand gestures. Both classification methods utilised the same sample dataset and camera input to achieve a fair comparison. Then, the performance in terms of accuracy and processing time being analysed. The results indicate that the CNN excels in recognising hand gestures with an accuracy of 97.78% compared to the SVM with 96.30%. In terms of processing time to train/process the datasets, SVM has the upper hand by taking 5 minutes and 16 seconds. Meanwhile the CNN used 8 minutes and 24 seconds.

articleTitle: LightRing-MO: Light Sensor Static-Authentication Using a Semi-Biometric Interacting with a LightRing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: At this time, the smartphone is one of the most popular and commonly utilized instruments for protecting private information. One of the smartphone authentication methods is biometrics. Yet, the age difference (i.e., the elderly versus children) impacts the validation technique. Derealization and amnesia are the most critical issues many confront when validating sensor-based behavioral and physical biometrics. This study suggests a novel authentication method for smartphones called LightRing-MO that uses a light source with a valid value (a ring controlling a light source) and is based on static authentication. It works by processing the luminometer sensor found in mobile smartphones. A smartphone luminometer may be used to show how the authentication process works while disclosing specific information for each light ring. Numerous users may be able to utilize the light intensity, and the light value may provide a wide range of authentication options. It is difficult to reproduce due of each user’s unique lightness value. The three participants—two adults and one child—exhibited a high accuracy rate of 98.33% throughout the trials thanks to their previous training. The next stage is to enlist additional individuals to investigate and thoroughly examine the implications of this approach.

articleTitle: Vision System for Recognition of Water Level, Rain Water and Flood Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: Several flood detection techniques have been designed to accurately measure water levels around the environment as a means to mitigate accidents or to be prepared for such scenarios. This paper presents a system that detects water levels and floods within the 2 surveillance cameras. Gathered images were trained into the YOLOv5 algorithm, enabling the system to recognize floods. By operating at a few seconds of intervals, the system can notify users if the water levels are rising around the area. This study concludes that the most optimal position and camera to be used for this study is the outdoor camera, showing better results as seen from the gathered data.

articleTitle: Development of a Smart Convenience Outlet with Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) Reader and Android Application for Power Monitoring, Control, and Protection of Electrical Home Appliances
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: This study presents a system that features power consumption monitoring per user, timer control, budget limit, automatic shutdown of standby appliances and provides protection from overloading, overvoltage and undervoltage. The prototype can be activated via an RFID card or mobile application. Each user has an account, and each account has a respective registered RFID card. The account and RFID card enable user identification which can aid in the fair distribution of electricity consumption and bill among roommates or users in an apartment or dormitory based on their actual appliance usage. A generated report is provided for both the users and the landlord. The system used PZEM-004T for measuring voltage and current. The percentage error computation was done on the current reading of the prototype and the clamp meter, in which the system has 95.15% to 99.94% accuracy in terms of current reading. On the other hand, the system has 99.30% to 99.90% accuracy in terms of voltage reading, in which the system voltage reading is compared to the reading of a multimeter. Given these features, the prototype can reduce excessive use of appliances, promotes fair distribution of electricity bill, and provides protection for overvoltage, undervoltage and overloading.

articleTitle: Identifying the Performance of Porous Silicon Based Humidity Sensors at Different Gold Contact Pad Spacings
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)

authors.preferredName: Wan Nur Sabrina Wan Ahmad Aziz

abstract: In recent years, porous silicon (PSi) substrate has been broadly studied by other researchers for microelectronics development due to its viable physical and chemical stability qualities. However, most of the studies published were primarily concerned with the synthesis, characterization, and uses of PSi. The influence of varying metal contact pad distances on humidity sensing performance was discovered to be rarely addressed in the current day. Therefore, this paper aims to investigate the influence of gold (Au) contact pad spacing on PSi in terms of the sensitivity and stability performance of humidity sensor application. In this study, PSi is synthesised via anodization and annealed at 250°C for 1 hour prior to humidity testing. The crystallinity of PSi was characterized using x-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis, which revealed a strong intensity of Si substrate diffraction peak at 69.3° (400) and a minor peak of cubic SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> at 33.1° (111) with low crystallinity. The sensor was tested for humidity detection in the 40% to 90% RH range using different contact gaps. Based on the results, the largest contact gap of 8.5 mm demonstrated the greatest sensitivity performance and output stability in comparison to the shorter contact gaps. The effect of varying the gap was visible in the current versus time graph of each RH level, with a significant decline in the device’s sensitivity as the gap decreased. Thus, our results imply that the emission area expands as the gap width widens due to the increased availability of oxygen vacancies and active sites for electron mobility.

articleTitle: Design of an Automatic Hybrid Battery-Powered Solar Box Cooker
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: In this paper, the researchers were able to design a hybrid solar box cooker wherein a battery is used to power the heating coil when sunlight is not enough, or when it is nighttime already. Because the solar box cooker alone is not effective enough, a hybrid solar box cooker will be designed, integrated with a control system, while a Solar panel will be used to charge the battery. A control system was also developed where the timer and temperature can be set, and the system will automatically turn off the heating coil when it reaches the maximum temperature set to avoid overheating of the solar box cooker. Water and potatoes were boiled, and eggs and bacon were fried upon testing. The results of the experiments show that the hybrid solar box cooker is the most effective method to cook food with. The average efficiency of the solar box cooker acting alone, heating coil acting alone, and hybrid solar box cooker were 5.47%, 22.35%, and 40.24%, respectively.

articleTitle: Design and Performance of A Parabolic Concentrator Solar System embedded with IoT Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-axis tracking system of the parabolic concentrator solar system and remote solar monitoring system. The proposed approach is to motivate emerging technologies to reduce the dependency on fossil fuels and optimize existing systems to minimize energy consumption. Among the referenced renewable sources of energy, the sun, or sun-powered energy, is the most plentiful and sustainable source that substantially gives humans more energy than they need. The solar system’s effectiveness is a significant fuel source in the transition to clean energy creation, reducing this problem. Hence a parabolic concentrator is introduced, an electric generator with high-intensity irradiance using a dual-axis tracking system and embedded IoT monitoring system. Thus, collected validated data have recorded the voltage generated by the parabolic solar panel concentrator shape as the parameter used. The results prove that it produces 35% to 40% more than the flat surface. The results revealed that the recorded voltage ranges between 12V to 13V, and the temperature when the sunlight radiance vertically aligned on the solar panel is around 32–34C°; meanwhile, the surrounding humidity is around 65–79%.

articleTitle: Augmented Reality Apps on Electronic Devices for Education Using Image-based Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: Engineering education is evolving with technology and educational methods and techniques for teaching and learning need to be renewed as technology continuously develops. The conventional way of teaching and learning is becoming least effective today as students tend to lose their focus during lectures. This research presents the development of Augmented Reality (AR) on electronic devices for education with Android smartphones. 3D models with Augmented Reality marker were developed using multiple Vuforia and Blender 3D software. The AR mobile application was designed using Unity 3D. Image based technique was used to track and scan the AR marker and display five engineering devices with detailed information. Virtual Studio Code is used to program the UI from Unity 3D. Result presents successful mobile AR apps for the five devices which created a new environment for teaching and learning. Sampling of 32 students were tested using the AR apps that shows they are immersive to learn due to the interaction with the 3D model. Analysis presents the effectiveness of augmented reality in education with 75% vote very effective and 25% for medium effectiveness. The respondents also contribute opinions on implementing augmented reality in virtual classes with agreement at 87.5% to implement the AR. Overall, a positive response with 90% of the testers finding Augmented Reality is helpful and stimulating in todays and future education.

articleTitle: 3D Game-Based Approach to Learning Ancient Malay Heritage’s History
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a 3-Dimensional (3D) game highlighting the Ancient Malay culture and history for learning purposes for school children. Many popular digital games feature historical context and aspects. Hikayat Hang Tuah is based on real characters from the Malay Annals. Hang Tuah was a Malaccan royal court warrior during the reign of Sultan Mansur Shah in the 15th century; now embodies the ideal Malay subject and is a symbol of Malay nationalism to this very day. However, the most current generation of students is hardly aware of the history of Hang Tuah and have a lack of interest in learning history because they do not favor learning history from written and lengthy texts. This paper presents a qualitative approach that examines how pupils view history. Such impetuses correspond with the fourth target of the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals (SDG), which to provide quality education by ensuring inclusive and equitable quality education for all. To increase school kids’ interest in studying history, this paper also includes a 3D game that incorporates Malay history. In addition to providing entertainment, it is intended that this 3D game will serve as a platform for learning about the history of the state of Melaka under Sultan Mansur Shah.

articleTitle: LIDAR For Coastal Monitoring Study – A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: LIDAR is a well-known method for capturing points at extremely high resolution, but its resolution is insufficient for tasks like object recognition, façade categorization, and assessing the behavior of feature extraction in terms of edges, fractures, and changes. This review paper for coastal monitoring study uses the Terrestrial Laser Scanning (TLS) 3D LIDAR data cloud to extract linear features, locate and categorize fractures, and apply the line effect technique. Maybe shorten the time it takes to analyze data, manage a massive data TLS point systematically, eliminate irrelevant data, and investigate different LIDAR applications. Thus, with the addition of TLS 3D LIDAR coastal monitoring and Geographic Information System (GIS) application, user friendly understanding changes in natural disaster issues, coastline management efficiently, erosion prevention risk and subsequent action plans for decision makers or the general public are countered.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic (PV) Module Defect Image Classification Analysis Using EfficientNetV2 Architectures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: This paper presents a study of Photovoltaic (PV) module defect image classification using EfficientNetV2, the newest convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture. Five classes of defects were considered in the study: Broken Glass, Cracked Solar Cell, Gridline Corrosion, Normal, and Yellowing. The images were pre-processed and augmented to increase the diversity of the data. Current methods often take a long time since they manually capture and analyze thousands of images to look for errors and patterns in the modules. Furthermore, there is a lack of research that implemented EfficientNetV2 architectures in classifying defect images in PV modules. Therefore, the objective of this study is to classify and analyze the performance of EfficientNetV2 with two models; EfficientNetV2-S and EfficientNetV2-L, and identify which model gives the highest performance. The best performance model of EfficientNetV2 will be compared with other CNN architecture namely VGG16. The finding demonstrates that EfficientNetV2-S gives the highest performance with achieved 93.69% of accuracy, precision (93.75%), recall (93.36%), and F1-score (93.69%) when compared to VGG16 architecture.

articleTitle: Sequential Batch Control Design for Parallel Pulper Process Optimisation in a Paper Recycling Facility
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: Over the last few years, a steady increase has been recorded in waste delivery to recycling facilities. Paper plants face the challenge of separating recyclable paper products from waste materials. Recycling factories are expanding to accommodate new separation processes to meet the demand. High-density pulpers are used throughout the initial stages of the paper recycling process to transform recyclable paper into pulp. The waste materials that are present with paper in pulpers have undesirable effects on the paper-to-pulp breakdown performance during the agitation phases of pulping. Screening processes after pulping can separate usable pulp from waste.Not all parts of the paper are broken down into reusable pulp fibres. Some parts are rejected as waste. Landfill costs must be reduced by reducing the amount of reusable paper sent to landfills with waste. Increasing the product agitation time during pulper processes is needed for more efficient paper-to-pulp breakdown. This article focuses on implementing a new control design software framework for adding a new pulper to an existing pulper process.

articleTitle: On-street Parking Guidance System Based on Real Distance Optimization Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: Smart parking is an essential component of smart cities as it provides numerous benefits, including improving transportation systems’ efficiency, reducing traffic congestion, and enhancing residents’ quality of life. Real-time parking guidance systems are commonly used in private parking to increase safety and better use the available parking space. However, many countries, such as Morocco, have limited private parking, resulting in a significant percentage of on-street parking. Onstreet parking does not have designated parking slots, causing users to park their vehicles in a way that affects parking capacity. This paper proposes a solution to this problem by presenting a guidance system for parallel on-street parking with two perspectives: a bird’s-eye view and a high-view camera that captures images of vehicles from the side or top. Our suggested system utilizes a real-distances optimization method to guide users during the parking process. We utilized the YOLOv7 object detector and k-NN algorithm in this approach. Moreover, the system incorporates fuzzy logic to help it understand the situation and make decisions based on the distances and time of maneuvering.

articleTitle: Motor Vehicle Plate Recognition System for Philippine Law Enforcement Checkpoints Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: In most cities of the Philippines, numerous law enforcement checkpoints are stationed as a vital part of securing public order and road safety. As the country’s population grew, we saw a rise in the volume of vehicles on public roads. In areas where a checkpoint is located, the usual flow of traffic becomes congested while officers conduct their standard operating procedures in the verification of vehicles. This study focuses on the development of a motor vehicle plate recognition system for Philippine law enforcement checkpoints. You Only Look Once (YOLO) v4 was used to locate and detect motor vehicle plates through a video feed from an external camera installed in the local machine. OpenCV was used to preprocess the cropped images while Tesseract-OCR was used to extract the motor vehicle plate number as text. The extracted plate number was then used to retrieve the motor vehicle details from a local database. A mean Average Precision (mAP) of 97.67% was achieved after training the model. The experimental results and performance analysis of the study show that the proposed solution is capable of identifying motor vehicles through the recognition of motor vehicle plate numbers.

articleTitle: Advanced Safety Accident Analysis for Temperature Variation on Methanol Chemical Plant
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: Carbon capture and utilization (CCU) is the process of capturing carbon dioxide (CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) to be recycled for further usage. Captured CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> can be converted to several products which is one group being alcohols, such as methanol, to use as biofuels and other alternative and renewable sources of energy. The purpose of this paper is to investigate the effect of different temperature on methanol plant due to consequence accidents analysis in Papar, Sabah, Malaysia. This work investigated the possibility of (1) to identify chemical component’s mass and volume in the mixture for different temperature on methanol production and (2) to quantify the safety of methanol plant using distance and area plot threat analysis for different temperature. Based on the inherent safer concept, the increasing of the temperature will affect the plant safety. In this study, there have three plant condition which have the volume of 42 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and the pressure of 442 bar at outlet stream but with three different temperatures which are 220°C, 260°C, and 300°C. To model the process and determine the mass density of the mixture, mass fraction, and volume fraction, HYSYS software was utilized. ALOHA and MARPLOT tools were then used to determine the distance and area plot threat of toxicity, thermal radiation and overpressure. Results proved that Plant 1 with 220°C operating temperature has the farthest red zone distance and highest rate of fatalities (751 m and 56.6%), compare to Plant 2 and 3, coming from MeOH toxicity and MeOH BLEVE at night time, respectively. This study can be used to recommend suitable and safe location for methanol plant and its surrounding area.

articleTitle: Fractional-order PD Control of a Position Servo Using Nelder-Mead Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: Fractional-order PD controller was applied in this study to control a position servo. Fractional-order control was known to provide better stability and performance compared to its integer-order counterpart. However, fractional-order PD has more parameters to tune which make it more complicated to design. Nowadays, there are many tuning platforms available which make application of FOPD more convenience. In this study, we applied FOMCON toolbox to tune the FOPD with Nelder-Mead optimization method. Several performance criterions were investigated in this study including IAE and ISE. From the simulation, both criterions produced almost similar response if gain is fixed and only the order was optimized. Further investigation was conducted to evaluate the effect of the order towards output response of a position servo. It was found that, as the order is decreased, the overshoot increased.

articleTitle: Analysis on the Effect of DC Current Changes on the Magnetic Field of Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: The generation of electromagnetic radiation in a solenoid, driven by alternating current (AC) voltage, is directly influenced by the voltage and current flowing through the solenoid. Exploiting this concept, wireless power transfer (WPT) systems can be developed. These systems consist of a sending coil and a receiving coil, both equipped with solenoids. The sending coil is connected to a half bridge circuit to generate AC voltage, which is then transmitted to the receiver coil. In this study, the effects of various factors on the performance of the wireless power transfer system were investigated, with a particular focus on the impact of DC voltage and input DC current. To examine these effects, an experimental setup was employed where the transmitter and receiver coils were powered by a DC voltage source. By varying the voltage and current parameters, the study aimed to analyze their influence on the wireless power transfer process. The simulation results show that 100 V and 150 V of DC current will produce 36.54 A and 54.8 A of input DC current respectively with constant resistor 7.54×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup> Ω. The result shows that the input DC current is directly proportional with the magnetic field, AC current at sending and receiving coil, voltage at sending and receiving coil and AC power at receiving coil. Increasing the input DC current will increase the magnetic field, AC current at sending coil and receiver coil, voltage at transmitter coil and receiving coil and AC power at receiving coil and vice versa.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Leaf Blight Detection System Using Image Processing with Intrusion Notification via SMS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: The color of plant leaves is used as an indicator to detect leaf blight disease in plants using digital image processing. Early detection of leaf blight disease in plants allows proper protection to avoid the widespread of the disease. The general objective of this study was to design and develop a leaf blight detection system using image processing and a motion sensor with a laser tripwire alert system to detect intrusion and send SMS alerts. The data were randomly divided into three portions, with 75% being allocated as the training dataset, 22% as validation, and 3% as testing. The YOLOv5 object detection model was trained to detect leaf blight disease, resulting in a mean average precision of 38.80% (mAP 0.5) and 13.3% (mAP 0.5:0.95), with a precision of 56% and a recall of 37.90%. The low performance can be attributed to the low number of datasets involved, also, there were no essential steps carried out in image analysis that helped enhance the data in images namely, noise reduction, contrast enhancement, image resizing, color correction, and segmentation. To improve the performance of the system, an additional data enhancement in images may be implemented to simplify the image and easier to analyze namely, preprocessing, feature extraction, feature selection, and classification. Also, the use of additional prevailing algorithms namely, SVM + Deep Features, ANN, and Fast R-CNN can help improve the accuracy of results. In addition, the motion sensor and laser tripwire for detecting intrusions, have high accuracy rates of 90% and 95%, respectively. Furthermore, the motion sensor and GSM module responsiveness has an average of 6.54 seconds out of 20 trials while the tripwire sensor and GSM module responsiveness has an average of 6.53 seconds out of 20 trials as well.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Slope Stability using Finite Element Method (FEM) and Limit Equilibrium Method (LEM)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: The stability analysis of slopes is crucial for designing appropriate slope stabilisation methods based on the physical and engineering properties of the soil in the slope area. Slope stability is typically evaluated using the factor of safety (FOS) determined through the Limit Equilibrium Method (LEM). However, the Finite Element Method (FEM) has gained significant attention in geotechnical engineering for conducting comprehensive numerical slope stability analyses. By employing mathematical models and computational algorithms, engineers can simulate slope behaviour and predict stability more accurately and efficiently than traditional methods. Thus, this paper aims to analyse the FOS of slopes and identify the critical slip surface using the LEM and FEM performed by computer software. Two slope profiles were analysed using GEO5 for LEM and PLAXIS 2D for FEM. The findings were compared and discussed. The results show that the FEM generally yields higher FOS values, while the LEM provides slightly lower values. The shapes and locations of the critical slip circles are almost identical for each analysis and method. Overall, this comparative study is crucial in ensuring the validity of the performed analysis by utilising computer software to expedite the analysis and design of the suitable slope stabilisation method.

articleTitle: Study of Stress Distribution at the Inner Surface of Uncemented Total Hip Replacement (THR)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: Uncemented total hip replacement (THR) is a reconstructive surgery to improve the function of the diseased femoral hip. This replacement relies of press-fit technique which it is the most crucial part. This replacement is said to be successful by achieving the primary fixation which consequently lead to the secondary fixation through osseointegration. However, aseptic loosening often reported case for this replacement where many patients need to have revision. There are reasons to believe that the high stress distribution at the bone inner surface leads to the implant failure. Therefore, this study aims to determine the stress distribution at the inner surface of the implanted femoral bone. A standardized femoral bone was generated from Initial Graphics Exchange Specification (IGES) format file. The bone model was then implanted and analyzed by using ANSYS Workbench (V15) Software. The femoral bone was having Young’s modulus of 14, 200 MPa and Poisson’s ratio of 0.3. Meanwhile, the material of the hip prosthesis used was Titanium (Ti-6A1-4V) which having Young’s modulus of 100, 000 MPa and Poisson’s ratio of 0.3. The implanted bone was subjected to walking load case. The results of the stress distribution for whole inner surface of the implanted bone were 56.02 MPa which below the failure stress.

articleTitle: Solar Powered Landslide Detection Using Global System Mobile (GSM) Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)

authors.preferredName: Muhammad Aiman Hakimi Bin Mohd Nong

abstract: Landslides are a big disaster that occurs all over the world every year, killing thousands of people. It is also the second-worst disaster in terms of devastation. Despite the increased awareness of the landslide problem, there is still a shortage of technologies created to reduce the probability of landslide occurrence. Existing technologies are very complex as well as costly. The local government campaign did not do enough to raise knowledge about how to prepare for landslides and how to mitigate their effects. There are technologies to monitor landslide risk, as well as proposals for activities to address existing difficulties and challenges related to landslide risk. There is a shortage of technology in Malaysia when it comes to landslides, as well as restricted costs and resources. Therefore, this project will develop a Global System for Mobile Communication (GSM) for landslide early warning system that will inform people to the possibility of a landslide so that they may take action and mitigate the damage. The methodology used in this project is a Global System for Mobile Communication (GSM), Arduino Uno, soil moisture sensor and gyro sensor, which are extremely useful in detecting the likelihood of landslides. The system efficacy and resilience were assessed throughout the project using a slope model and data collection. The system was test on the created slope model and the experimental result shows that the system was able to send an early warning of landslide via GSM based on the sensors detection. The objective of the project has been achieved and the project is working as planned.

articleTitle: Nutrient Deficiency Classification using AlexNet Architecture
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: Oil palm significantly contributes to Malaysia’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP). To maintain palm oil productivity, keeping the oil palm crop in good health, and free from nutrient deficiencies is necessary. Therefore, a method to analyze nutrient deficiencies is required. Nutrient deficiencies can be detected in the oil palm leaves. The study proposes an image-processing method that classifies three crucial nutrient deficiencies in a palm oil leaf: Nitrogen, Potassium, and Magnesium. To improve the processing rate, a convolution neural network (CNN) based on the AlexNet architecture has been implemented, which has been successful in image classification tasks and produced remarkable results in automated classification. The AlexNet architecture consists of five (5) convolved layers and three (3) fully connected layers, achieving an accuracy of 90.85%. This shows that AlexNet is an efficient algorithm for classifying nutrient deficiencies in palm oil leaves. However, a lower classification rate was observed for Magnesium compared to Nitrogen and Potassium. Due to the similarity in texture and color which may cause misinterpretation by the classifier. Further exploration of other CNN architectures will be conducted in the future to improve classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Optimizing Gas Production Forecasting in Iraq Using a Hybrid Artificial Intelligence Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: This paper aims to enhance the accuracy and reliability of gas production predictions for Iraq until 2030 by comparing traditional time series methods (ARIMA) with a hybrid artificial intelligence (AI) model that combines artificial neural networks (ANN) and genetic algorithms (GA). The integration of ANN and GA aims to leverage the strengths of pattern recognition and parameter optimization for more precise forecasting. The study’s objectives revolve around contributing to sustainable development goals within Iraq’s energy sector. The research methodology encompasses data collection, preprocessing, training ANN models, optimizing parameters using GA, and evaluating the hybrid approach’s performance. The results of this research will provide valuable insights for policymakers and industry stakeholders, empowering them to make informed decisions aligned with sustainable development objectives.

articleTitle: Layer of Protection Analysis (LOPA) as an Effective Tool for Preventing Major Accidents Hazards: A Case Study of Ammonia Storage Tank
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: Major accidents in process industry still occur until now. Some of the major accidents are the Bhopal Disaster in 1984 and Deepwater Horizon in 2010. The most recent major accident in Malaysia, is at PETRONAS facility in Pengerang, Johor where there was an explosion and fire. Layer of protection analysis or well known as LOPA, is a simplified risk assessment tool used to examine hazards. Research, process development, design, operations, maintenance, alterations, and decommissioning all benefit from LOPA. LOPA involves identifying the target risk levels, determining the existing risk connected to the process, and choosing the best non-instrumented safety systems. The major accident prevention and control strategies in the chemical process sector will be uncovered in this research. The effectiveness of layer of protection analysis (LOPA) in preventing significant accidents in high-risk chemical plants is another objective of the study. The layer of protection analysis (LOPA) will be studied when adequate data for preventative and control actions has been acquired. The starting frequency and failure rate statistics will be obtained. For each layer of LOPA, the efficiency of preventing significant accidents will be determined by calculation.

articleTitle: The Implementation of Mobile Application Ordering System to Optimize The User Experience of Food and Beverage Industry
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: Nowadays, online ordering has become a fairly widespread phenomenon, and consumers are aiming for efficient buying experiences. This study will cover the problems with online ordering that businesses encounter, as well as the problems with emailing order confirmations and the inability to send messages to several users at once. These problems will be resolved by creating a smartphone application for ordering food online. Due to the prevalence of smartphones and people’s preference for using their phones for tasks, this study will be focusing on implementing mobile application ordering system to optimize the user experience of food and beverage industry. After the mobile application has been developed, it is made available to Android users for download and testing of the user interface and email functions. As part of user interface and functional testing, the team will locate a few respondents who have not utilized the mobile application. The team will distribute surveys on the user experience to respondents after the users have finished the test so they can offer feedback. This survey is meant to check if the mobile application could perform all related email-blast tasks, including properly sending and receiving emails to multiple users at once, and can live up to user expectations for order confirmation. A user satisfaction survey is conducted to record the user’s perceptions of the usability, usefulness, and satisfaction of the mobile application’s features. The online ordering function will be applicable to all types of businesses, allowing them to improve their performance and expand their popularity.

articleTitle: Parkinson’s Disease Symptom Detection using Hybrid Feature Extraction and Classification Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: In recent years, there has been a significant demand for diagnosing and monitoring various neurological-based disease diseases such as Parkinson’s disease. This study aims to develop a web-based symptom detector that can predict Parkinson’s disease at an early stage. Users can either draw or upload a spiral image on the website for analysis. To achieve this, the study proposes a hybrid model that combines the Histogram of Oriented Gradients Descriptor and Random Forest Classifier. Features are being extracted from a series of spiral drawings, which serve as the dataset, and then classifies the extracted data using the proposed model. The achieved results show an average accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity of 83.33%, 73.33%, and 93.33% respectively. In conclusion, this approach demonstrates promising potential for early detection of Parkinson’s disease using the proposed web-based symptom detector.

articleTitle: The Development of Travel Mobile Application for Local Malaysian Tourism Destinations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: Users of travel applications can arrange services that are referred to as “m-Travelling” by researching places, locating affordable flights and lodging, and booking such services. It is found that there is a current gap in the market for a comprehensive and user-friendly platform that promotes domestic tourism meanwhile get accurate information easily. Most travel apps also expect their users to have stable and strong internet connections and the apps are found to be not user-friendly. The aim of this study is to develop a travel application for tourism sites in the Selangor area. Data were collected from local citizens of Selangor and local travellers that travel a lot in Malaysia. It was found that most of the respondents were experienced with travel mobile apps and most of them were neutral with the problems faced as the casualties may not drastically affect the user experience throughout the usage of travel apps. This study concludes that the development of travel mobile applications can be an effective way to support Malaysian tourism destinations and promote domestic tourism, encouraging to exploration of appreciation the local culture, heritage, and natural beauty to provide users with a convenient and accessible platform. The apps include information about local attractions, hotels, restaurants, transportation, and other essential travel services. Overall, the development of a travel mobile application for local Malaysian tourism destinations will promote cultural awareness and appreciation and provide users with an enjoyable and memorable travel experience through social technological developments.

articleTitle: Comparative Review on Traditional and Deep Learning Methods for Medical Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: Medical image segmentation is a vital task in medical imaging, aiming to extract meaningful and precise information from images. While traditional methods have been extensively used, they often suffer from drawbacks like poor accuracy and robustness. In contrast, deep learning methods, with their promising results in various applications, including medical image segmentation, are compared in this literature review. The review highlights the strengths and limitations of both approaches, providing insights into the current state-of-the- art techniques. Ultimately, it concludes that deep learning methods have demonstrated superior performance in medical image segmentation and are anticipated to make a significant impact in this field.

articleTitle: Optimizing Sports Center Recommendation System in Malaysia Through Content-Based Filtering Technique and Web Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: Sports center is a place that provides services for sports court booking where people can play the sport together as a group of families or friends. However, with the traditional method of booking, which needs to book directly at the venue, many customers feel unsure about which sports court is available provided by the sports center because there are no recommendations. Thus, a new method is needed to recommend the customer according to their preferences: Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency and Cosine Similarity technique. This study proposed these methods for optimizing the sports center’s recommendation system, and both are content-based filtering. It is implemented using a web-based platform. Two types of testing were conducted: functionality and cosine similarity testing that tested for user profile, location and court. As a result, the functional testing results showed all requirements correctly and successfully. The cosine similarity score for the user profile location for Test 1 is between 0.2894 and 0.5031; meanwhile, Test 2 is between 0.2781 and 0.4557. The similarity between the court and location is 1.0. It shows that the details of the sports center recommendation are similar to the features input and correctness. Therefore, it can conclude that optimizing the sports center recommendation system through content-based filtering enables the customer to choose the sports center with the similarity features based on the user’s latest booking of location and court in the system.

articleTitle: Survey: Gait Recognition Based on Image Energy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: Gait, a biometric trait, is a highly valuable indicator that enables the identification of an individual from a significant distance and without requiring direct physical contact. Due to its unique attributes that are absent in other commonly used identifiers such as fingerprints and iris recognition, gait recognition has become increasingly prevalent and widely adopted in various areas where it is feasible to utilize video reconnaissance frameworks. As computer vision techniques have advanced, there are now numerous methods for recognizing individuals through their movements in the video, utilizing both traditional biometric characteristics such as the human skeleton, its silhouette, and its changes during walking, as well as unique signals. This paper explores the use of gait energy extraction as a fundamental approach for discriminating between different gaits, an analysis of the classification algorithms employed, and a comparison of the methods based on accuracy, gait datasets, as well as their characteristics, issues, and challenges encountered in the development of gait recognition systems. and identified the prevailing methods employed by researchers as GEI (Gait Energy Image) and FDF(Frequency Domain Feature ). Followed by GENI (Gait Entropy Image), CGI (Chrono-Gait Image ), and GFI(Gait Flow Image ). Among the available datasets, CASIA and OU-ISIR as the most extensively used and comprehensive datasets in the field. Using convolutional neural networks, they demonstrated that CGI achieved the highest level of accuracy when applied to the CASC-B dataset.

articleTitle: A Review Study of an Intelligent Strategy Towards Higher Education Examination Management Structure Based on Fog Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: Universities currently employ manual and partial digital methods for managing examinations, which involve extensive paperwork and consume significant time. This approach raises significant issues, such as time-consuming processes, errors, poor exam and result quality, submission delays, plagiarism, inaccurate grading, and a lack of security. Lecturers face challenges when creating exam questions for every subject every semester, often reusing previous questions without considering their quality, failing educational quality standards. The marking of exam scripts is often rushed to meet deadlines, leading to substandard grading, and the entire process is time-consuming and requires unnecessary effort. Un considerable amount of paper is utilized, and the storage of exam scripts occupies substantial physical space, posing the risk of damage or loss. A novel approach was proposed via Intelligent Green Examination Structure based on fog computing to address these issues. This innovative structure aims to transform traditional examination procedures into an automated, intelligent, and secure system that reduces human involvement and ensures high-quality outcomes. This research focuses on evaluating the effectiveness of an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered digital exam management structure based on Fog Computing in enhancing the efficiency and security of exam administration. The structure of this paper begins with a problem discussion, hypothesis, objectives, significance of the research, literature review, and research methodology.

articleTitle: Rust Detection on Galvanized Iron Sheets using Convolutional Neural Network and Mask R-CNN
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: Rust in galvanized iron sheets poses problems with the structural quality of the sheet. It is important that regular maintenance and monitoring are employed to prevent further deterioration and hazards. Smart methods have emerged in structural maintenance and monitoring through computer technology. This study aimed to classify rust based on visibility using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and locate rust using Mask Region-based Convolutional Neural Network (Mask R-CNN). To do this, a manually acquired and custom rust dataset was built and categorized into No Rust, Slightly Visible Rust, Visible Rust, and Heavy Visible Rust. The custom dataset was built with the guidance of an expert on the subject matter and was validated and verified. In this study, CNN obtained 80% accuracy on the test set. Mask R-CNN obtained an Average Precision with a threshold of 50% (AP50) value of 70.958% on its box parameter and an AP50 value of 70.139% on its segment parameter. The prototype was also tested under different lighting intensities, and it was found that the classification and localization performance had improved and became more consistent when light intensities reached 160,000 lux.

articleTitle: The Digital Documentations of Historical Charcoal Chamber Monument Using LiDAR Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: Conventional methods in the work of documenting historical objects practice the use of paper filing methods where pictures of historic objects are recorded as hard copies. This method is vulnerable to destruction due to the materials used. This paper describes the use of LiDAR technology for the documentation of historical object known as historical charcoal chamber. The historical charcoal chamber is one of the historical monuments located at Kubak Badak Geotrail, Langkawi Island geopark area, claimed to be approximately 150 years old. It was made by the bricks and were used to create coals from the woods from the surrounding mangrove trees. The methodology of the research begins with data collection process. The LiDAR technology used for the data collection process is a terrestrial LiDAR known as Topcon GLS2000. The scanning process involved four scanning stations with medium scanning resolutions. The second part of the methodology involved data pre-processing where the raw scanning data involved with registration and cleaning process. The post-processing part involved the generation of colored point clouds and the photo-realistic three-dimensional model of the charcoal chamber. This paper also shows how the 3D model of the charcoal chamber historic object is used to predict the full shape of the historic charcoal chamber which can be used in history subject education in the future.

articleTitle: WAN Internet Traffic Parameter Analysis on Metro-E Campus Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: This paper presents a parameter analysis of WAN internet traffic on a Metro-E campus network that addressed the network congestion and delay issues in network Quality of Service (QoS) bandwidth management. Recently, internet traffic has been gradually increasing which results in bandwidth bursts that affect network QoS. The method involves analyzing data collected over 12 months on the Metro-E 100Mbps campus network using Exinda Network Orchestrator. The result presents heavy-tailed distributions on an inbound packet kurtosis value of 347 and an outbound packet kurtosis value of 780. Bytes outbound and inbound are skewed at 122 and right at 17 accordingly. The average amount of data inbound and outbound is 458.5MB and 34.8MB. A weak positive correlation at 0.0284 exists between the maximum inbound and maximum outbound throughput on the network. The correlation coefficient’s 95% confidence interval ranges between 0.021 to 0.035. However, a strong positive correlation at 0.985 between inbound intervals and outbound intervals, and the correlation coefficient’s 95% confidence interval ranges between 0.984 to 0.985 This research is significant in the future deployment of traffic scheduling, policing, and shaping algorithms for QoS bandwidth management on the WAN Metro-E campus network. This study has implications for Wan Metro-E Network traffic scheduling, policing traffic, and future QoS shaping.

articleTitle: COVID-19 Lung Detection using Keras Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: A novel coronavirus, known as COVID-19, is a recently discovered virus that primarily affects the upper respiratory tract and lungs. With the global pandemic reaching alarming proportions, the number of cases and fatalities continues to rise. In the medical field, chest X-ray images have emerged as a valuable tool for monitoring various lung disorders, including COVID-19. This research focuses on leveraging deep learning techniques, specifically convolutional neural networks (CNN) implemented with Keras, to accurately identify COVID-19 and normal chest X-ray images. The study involves feature extraction, fine-tuning of pretrained CNN models (VGG19, ResNet50V2, Xception, MobileNetV2, and DenseNet121), and training of a customized CNN model. The aim is to evaluate and compare the performance of these models in detecting COVID-19 lung abnormalities. The dataset consists of 455 images, including 221 COVID-19 chest X-ray images and 234 normal chest X-ray images. Accuracy testing is used to assess the classification performance of the research. The experimental results demonstrate that deep learning models have the capability to effectively detect COVID-19 from chest X-ray images. These proposed models can serve as a foundation for future work, such as predicting accuracy and advancing diagnostic capabilities.

articleTitle: Tuning of PID Controller Based on Tasmanian Devil Optimization for Unmanned Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of disturbances experienced by unmanned aerial vehicles and unmanned underwater vehicles. It aims to achieve speed tracking and disturbance rejection using an efficient control method. To manage speed under various disturbance conditions, a novel metaheuristic bio-inspired algorithm known as Tasmanian Devil Optimization (TDO) is used to optimize the parameters of the Proportional Integral Derivative (PID) controller. The performance of TDO is compared to that of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Ant Colony Optimization (ACO). According to the simulation results obtained using MATLAB/Simulink, the TDO outperforms the PSO and ACO in terms of the characteristics of speed response.

articleTitle: Application of SVM Classification Technique in Single-phase AC Motor Bearing Fault Diagnosis using Motor Current Analysis with MRA - FFT as Feature Extractor and CFFS as Feature Selection Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: Induction motors dominate a significant part of the industry since it is the most well-known type of motor used in industrial, commercial, and domestic contexts. Considering the harsh conditions in most industrial environments, induction motors are frequently prone to issues such as bearing faults. This study proposes a real-time bearing fault-diagnostic model for a single-phase AC motor using a data acquisition device made from Arduino Uno R3 and SCT-013-030 current sensor. Machine learning algorithms such as Multiresolution Analysis and Fast Fourier Transform (MRA-FFT) as feature extractor, Correlation and Fitness values-based Feature Selection (CFFS) as a feature selection method, and Support Vector Machine (SVM) as classification technique were also applied in this study to evaluate the performance of the proposed bearing fault detection model. Results showed that for the training and validation (80:20), the best accuracy is 89.39% at the SNR level of infinite dB. And for testing the performance of the trained bearing diagnostic model using the confusion matrix, the best accuracy is 88% for the SNR level of infinite dB.

Author Keywords: Correlation and Fitness values-based Feature Selection

articleTitle: Analyzing Social Distancing Compliance Through YOLOv3: A Framework for Parameters Violation Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)

authors.preferredName: Nur Nayli Maisarah Bt Mohd Zapuan

abstract: This paper proposes the utilization of the You Only Look Once (YOLO) object detection model as a deep learning method to monitor the implementation of social distancing as a preventive measure against highly infectious diseases. The objective is to determine the suitability of YOLO by conducting a literature review and comparing it with other object detection models, including Faster Region Based-Convolutional Neural Network (R-CNN) and Single Shot Detector (SSD). The paper aims to evaluate the models based on metrics such as mean average precision (mAP), frames per second (FPS), and loss values, in order to assess the effectiveness of the proposed approach. The comprehensive testing conducted in this study confirms that the YOLO model is highly suitable for social distancing monitoring detection. Its precise object detection capabilities, coupled with efficient processing, make a significant scientific contribution to preventing the spread of highly infectious diseases by monitoring social distancing compliance.

articleTitle: An Assessment of Method for Sedimentation Area Detection at Kuala Perlis Using Landsat 8 OLI within the Year 2019 to 2021
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: Sedimentation at the river mouth always occurs in Kuala Perlis disrupting the ferries and boat users, especially during the low tide. This study is aimed to compare the best method for predicting river sediment deposition between K-Means unsupervised image classification machine learning and Modified Normalized Difference Water Index (MNDWI) in analyzing the areas most influenced by depositing river sediments from the clustered images. Quantification of Landsat 8 OLI satellite images were applied using ENVI software in the study area to detect sedimentation utilizing image data band correlation deposited river sediment through the unsupervised classifier algorithm and selection of spectral bands for MNDWI. The determination of determinant bands from analysis of correlation coefficient resulted in NIR bands for their lowest R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> coefficient that ranged from 0.5 to 0.7. Then the selected K-Means classification method has been taken for further clustered image analysis compared to the MNDWI method. From the analysis through stage statistic, visual observation and previous studies review, the river sediment deposition at the river mouth was significantly increased from the year 2019 to the year 2021. These results were supported by the 14 percent of the increase for riverbed regions subjected to sediment deposition with R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> 0.916. The location of Kuala Perlis itself exacerbated the problem of dumping sediment returned to the river mouth in a brief period, which is also reliant on the wave flow. This study exhibits importance results for the future development of Kuala Perlis and local communities nearby.

articleTitle: Bibliometric Analysis using Cytochrome P450 (CYP51) Data Between 1980–2018 for BigData and Blockchain in Biomedical Research
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: Information sciences is a wide field of study using information in the form of data or text which can be arranged or categorized using pattern recognition whether mathematically via algorithms or by subject matter to better understand a topic of interest. Here this study uses Cytochrome P450 enzyme, a sterol demethylase (CYP51) publication data as the subject matter to understand collaboration between 1980 and 2018. This paves the way for bigdata and blockchain in biomedical research. Sterol demethylase CYP51 published journal articles includes research articles, reviews, technical notes and reports related to all kingdoms of life. This study uses priori thematic analysis method of CYP51 published literature focusing on authors, geographical areas and selected kingdoms of life. Purposive sampling method was used to collect the data from scientific databases. Data source triangulation was employed involving different data search to gain multiple validation of results. It was found 504 published articles have met the inclusion criteria. Overall, this study showed that a total of 2454 authors were involved in CYP51 research and majority are located in North America region. This bibliographic analysis (BA) outlined rough case-study approach on data searching options for organisms which may be expanded into studies of wider kingdoms, regions and organisms using data analytics algorithms advances.

articleTitle: Feature Extraction and Signature Classification for Non-Intrusive Appliance Load Monitoring using High Frequency Data
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: Electricity usage has become a crucial aspect of daily life in both urban and rural areas worldwide. Non-Intrusive Appliance Load Monitoring (NIALM) system is to identify energy consumption and disaggregate loads for each home appliances from the total aggregated energy usage. Prior works use signal processing and statistical pattern recognition techniques to decompose the energy consumption. However, the highly compute intensive techniques are evolving with advanced algorithms for the analysis. This paper explores the feature extraction from in-house appliance recorded dataset, performs signature classification with Machine Learning and analyzes the impact of the individual features on the model performance. It involves summarizing high-frequency data and employing the resulting summary data to train five appliance signature models. The evaluation result shows it achieves a satisfactory accuracy of 89%. However, the unperformed model only reaches 38% of accuracy. Furthermore, the contribution of the features towards the models assesses using SHAP Analysis on two models.

articleTitle: Water Quality Detection System using Real Time Vision Computing with Trash Collector
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: The increasing pace of industrialization and population has led to an ever-increasing demand for water, accompanied by a rise in water pollution levels. While industrial growth brings economic stability to nations, it has profound consequences for environmental resources. Both renewable and non-renewable resources are exploited to manufacture industrial products, resulting in the production of non-degradable waste that is frequently discarded into water bodies. This research focuses on finding a viable solution to reduce river water pollution and promote awareness of river quality. The proposed solution involves the development of a water quality detection system that utilizes real-time vision computing and a litter collector to monitor water quality and collect floating debris on the water surface. The system is designed with a centralized microcontroller (Arduino Mega) acting as the control center, transmitting data to a cloud-based monitoring platform. It is integrated into the litter collector, equipped with a surveillance camera for safety during debris collection. The microcontroller also controls the movement of the Seabin using a radio frequency controller. Through the integration of an Arduino program, this research has achieved significant outcomes by enabling simultaneous monitoring of multiple water quality parameters and offering control capabilities through the frequency controller.

articleTitle: Progression of Artificial Pancreas Device System Development with Preliminary Comparison between Two Models for Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM) Patients
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM) typically results from autoimmune β cell destruction, causing the blood glucose level (BGL) to exceed or be less than the normoglycemic condition. Generally, it is because the pancreas cannot produce enough insulin to stimulate the transport of glucose from the plasma into adipose tissue and muscle. There is vast research for T1DM management using a variety of diabetic models which help regulate the BGL to deliver the correct amount of insulin. Amongst the diabetic models which have relative ease to be used are the UVA/PADOVA simulator and the Hovorka model. Nevertheless, a comparison between the UVA/PADOVA simulator and the Hovorka model with virtual data from UVA/PADOVA simulator is unavailable. This study uses a quantitative method by collecting data for T1DM patients in UVA/PADOVA simulator for 3 virtual patients. The diabetic model using Hovorka equations via MATLAB R2022a were simulated to run the T1DM patient’s data for carbohydrates consumed during breakfast, lunch, and dinner. This study acts as a preliminary effort to compare in-silico work from the Hovorka model to the UVA/PADOVA simulator for output results of BGL and optimum insulin injection to keep the normoglycemic condition for T1DM patients. The results show that the BGL versus time graph using the Hovorka model with the numerical method such as Runge-Kutta and Euler methods gave a higher peak point for patients in BGL for the Hovorka model and UVA/PADOVA simulator. The data for each patient was similar to each other. The trend of the BGL level for the Hovorka model reduces steadily after insulin injection during a meal consumed by T1DM patients. The amount of insulin injection was identified by trial and error to get a normoglycemic condition. In conclusion, the Hovorka model is a simple method that can be used by T1DM to control their BGL.

articleTitle: Biometric Authentication Utilizing EEG Based-on a Smartphone’s 3D Touchscreen Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: Recently, smartphone manufacturers have begun including large storage capacities and powerful processors. Users’ personal lives, professional lives, and vast multimedia collections are all kept on their smartphones. Personal identification numbers (PINs), passwords, biometric data, gestures, and patterns are used extensively by these mobile phones. However, these mechanisms have numerous security flaws and are vulnerable to attacks, including shoulder surfing. Electroencephalography (EEG) signals are one of a kind, and this fact can be used to overcome the shortcomings of currently used methods. These signals can be captured and sent via wireless channels to be processed. In this research, we present a novel security system for mobile devices that combines the 3D touch authentication offered by 3DTPT with EEG signals. The authentication credentials based on 3D patterns are considered identification tokens. We have considered using EEG signals captured during a three-level pattern drawing over the smartphone’s screen as part of the authentication procedure. To do so, we recorded the brain activity of 10 participants as they drew one of three distinct patterns. The system’s security was tested by simulating 25 unsuccessful attempts by five malicious users to break in using the same methods as five legitimate users. A Hidden Markov Model (HMM) models EEG signals, and a Support Vector Machine (SVM) binary classifier verifies test pattern reliability. The DET, HTER, and ROC curves are security matrices used to evaluate verification systems. Positive experimental findings suggest this method has potential as an alternative to developing sophisticated authentication systems for mobile devices.

articleTitle: Quality of Leaves Classification Using CNN
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th Control and System Graduate Research Colloquium (ICSGRC)
abstract: This study demonstrates the incredible benefits of information technology (IT) to agriculture by demonstrating how well Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with dropout can be used to classify the quality of rubber tree seedlings through their leaves. The researcher has gone through every fundamental step such as pre-processing, structuring of the model, training and evaluation of the model, and producing classification report. Data augmentation has been applied to increase the number of data sample during the training of CNN and it gives 96% accurate result for new images. It was noticed that during the evaluation of the model it posted 98% accuracy result in classifying the data with the same procedure set during the training the model. However, the classification report of each data sample that is not included in the datasets of training and evaluation.
